story.title: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
story.summary: An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport after overrunning the runway, resulting in five fatalities and five injuries. The incident occurred when the plane, arriving from Puerto Rico, struck several vehicles on the ground. Investigations by the FAA and NTSB are underway to determine the cause of the crash.

explore_lenses.label: Why did one crash disrupt so much travel?
explore_lenses.title: A runway closure at a major cargo-and-passenger hub
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate safety response closed MIA's runways and taxiways, producing effects far beyond the crash site. MIA's unusually large passenger and freight volume makes a prolonged disabled-aircraft response nationally consequential.

claims.text: Miami-Dade Aviation said all runways and taxiways were closed after the overrun, and the FAA imposed a ground stop while emergency crews responded.
As of late September 6, the FAA reported average arrival delays into MIA of more than six hours because of the disabled aircraft.
MIA handled about 55.3 million passengers, 3.4 million freight tons, and nearly 499,000 commercial aircraft movements in 2025, according to the airport operator.

explore_lenses.label: Who is accountable for the flight?
explore_lenses.title: Amazon branding, but a separate aircraft operator
explore_lenses.summary: The aircraft was operating in Amazon's Prime Air network, but Amazon identified 21 Air as the operator. That distinction matters because a safety investigation can examine the carrier's flight and maintenance operations alongside airport, aircraft and network-related evidence.

claims.text: The FAA identified the aircraft as a Boeing 767-300 arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico; Miami-Dade Aviation identified it as a Prime Air aircraft.
Amazon said the aircraft was operated by 21 Air and that its priority was the safety, well-being and care of those involved while it worked with authorities.

The NTSB may designate technically qualified companies and agencies as parties to an investigation, but those parties may assist with fact-gathering only; the NTSB alone analyzes evidence and determines probable cause.

explore_lenses.label: What will the investigation need to establish?
explore_lenses.title: An overrun is known; its cause is not
explore_lenses.summary: The confirmed event is a landing runway overrun, not a determined explanation for it. Investigators will need to assess the circumstances of the landing and airport environment before attributing fault or recommending changes.

claims.text: The FAA defines a runway excursion as an aircraft veering off or overrunning the runway surface; it says such events can involve factors including approach stability and runway condition.

FAA guidance on landing-performance risk mitigation addresses braking reports, runway-condition assessments, landing-distance evaluation, and operator procedures—areas that can be relevant to a landing overrun but are not evidence of a cause in this case.

Forecast: the NTSB says a preliminary report is typically released within weeks, while a final report with probable cause commonly takes about one to two years; it cautions that preliminary facts should not be used to speculate about cause.

story_report.summary: A Prime Air cargo aircraft arriving at Miami International Airport from San Juan, Puerto Rico, overran the runway and struck vehicles, killing five people and injuring five others. The FAA identified the aircraft as a Boeing 767-300, while Miami-Dade Aviation identified it as a Prime Air aircraft. The crash prompted an emergency response, airport-wide operational closures and a federal investigation.

sections.heading: Airport Operations Face Severe Disruption
sections.body: Miami-Dade Aviation said all runways and taxiways were closed after the overrun, and the FAA imposed a ground stop as emergency crews responded. By late September 6, the FAA reported average arrival delays of more than six hours into MIA because of the disabled aircraft. The disruption affected a major aviation hub that handled about 55.3 million passengers, 3.4 million freight tons and nearly 499,000 commercial aircraft movements in 2025.

sections.heading: Amazon Operator and Investigation Process
sections.body: Amazon said the aircraft was operated by 21 Air and that its priority was the safety, well-being and care of those involved as it worked with authorities. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating. Under NTSB procedures, technically qualified companies or agencies may be designated to help gather facts, but the board alone analyzes the evidence and determines probable cause.

sections.heading: Federal Inquiry Will Examine Overrun
sections.body: The FAA defines a runway excursion as an aircraft veering off or overrunning the runway surface, and says such events can involve factors including approach stability and runway condition. FAA landing-performance guidance addresses braking reports, runway-condition assessments, landing-distance evaluations and operator procedures, though none establishes a cause in this crash. The NTSB says a preliminary report is typically released within weeks; a final report with probable cause commonly takes one to two years.

unresolved.text: The duration of airport restrictions and the full extent of cancellations or cargo disruption had not been established as of September 7.
No official cause had been established, including any conclusion about weather, aircraft performance, maintenance, crew actions, air traffic control or runway safeguards.
Public reporting had not identified where the victims were located, the aircraft registration, or the organizations formally designated by the NTSB as investigation parties.

related_stories.title: Indonesia Maintains Airport Closures Amid Easing Anak Krakatau Eruption
related_stories.summary: Indonesia has kept several airports closed due to the ongoing effects of the Anak Krakatau volcanic eruption, despite signs that the eruption is easing. The situation has led to the cancellation of hundreds of flights and stranded thousands of travelers. Indonesia, located along the Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' is home to more than 120 active volcanoes.

related_stories.title: UK Takes Steps Against Israeli Settlements Amid Rising Violence
related_stories.summary: The UK government is planning to implement new measures against illegal Israeli settlements as violence against Palestinians escalates. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has committed to a more decisive approach, including a proposed ban on trade with these settlements. A UN expert has welcomed this initiative but emphasizes the need for further action to ensure it has a meaningful impact.

related_stories.title: Israeli Strikes in Southern Lebanon Result in Multiple Casualties
related_stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on a southern Lebanese town have reportedly killed at least 11 people, including two infants and two medics, according to Lebanon's state news agency. This follows a separate incident where three individuals were killed in earlier strikes targeting Hezbollah infrastructure in response to an attempted attack on Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) troops. The recent escalation comes despite a ceasefire agreement established in June.
